guide_enrichment.narrative:
We understand the case for Wake Forest after an opener in which the offense produced 559 yards and committed no turnovers. Gio Lopez completed 21 of 32 passes for 350 yards and three touchdowns without an interception, while also adding 39 rushing yards. Those results show the offense has playmaking potential, but we are not treating one game against Akron as proof that the same efficiency will carry into this matchup.

Our longer-run numbers present a much tougher picture. Miami holds the advantage against both the run and pass, and its ability to prevent scoring opportunities is particularly important when evaluating whether Wake Forest can stay within the market's expectation. For us, the encouraging opener is balanced by matchup indicators that favor Miami, leaving our view essentially aligned with the current price and without enough value to justify a position.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Lopez and the Wake Forest passing game against Miami's pass defense. Carlos Hernandez has caught at least five passes in five consecutive games, and Wake Forest did not allow a sack in its opener, but our efficiency numbers still give Miami a clear advantage in this phase. If Miami limits explosive completions and forces Wake Forest to sustain drives, it becomes much harder for the home offense to outperform what the market is already pricing.

recent_game.fact: Wake Forest opened the 2026 season with a 38-16 home victory over Akron on Sept. 3.
Wake Forest produced 559 total yards against Akron, including 203 rushing yards and 356 passing yards.
Wake Forest converted 7 of 15 third downs and both of its fourth-down attempts against Akron.
Wake Forest committed no turnovers against Akron and recovered one Akron fumble.

quarterback.fact: North Carolina transfer Gio Lopez is Wake Forest's starting quarterback and one of six team captains.
In his Wake Forest debut against Akron, Lopez completed 21 of 32 passes for 350 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing seven times for 39 yards.
Lopez's 78-yard touchdown pass to Carlos Hernandez against Akron was the longest completion of his collegiate career.
Through the Akron game, Lopez's career totals were 438-of-666 passing for 5,131 yards, 35 touchdowns and 12 interceptions, plus 791 rushing yards and 12 rushing touchdowns.
Wake Forest's unofficial depth chart lists redshirt freshman Steele Pizzella as Lopez's backup.

offensive_personnel.fact: Weber State transfer Will Way is Wake Forest's starting center on the unofficial depth chart and was selected as a team captain.
Wake Forest's unofficial starting offensive line is Tolu Olajide at left tackle, Clinton Richard at left guard, Will Way at center, Ryan Berger at right guard and Aidan Martin at right tackle.
Ty Clark III made his third career start against Akron and rushed seven times for a career-high 105 yards, including a 57-yard run.
Carlos Hernandez caught five passes for 165 yards and a touchdown against Akron, including a 78-yard score.
Hernandez has caught at least five passes in each of Wake Forest's last five games, averaging 107.6 receiving yards with five touchdowns over that span.
Wake Forest's unofficial depth chart lists Hernandez, Antonio Meeks and Kam Shanks as the first-team wide receivers.

defensive_personnel.fact: Wake Forest's unofficial defensive front lists Langston Hardy and Gabe Kirschke at end, Dallas Afalava at defensive tackle and Zach Lohavichan at nose guard.
The unofficial depth chart lists Frank Cusano and Aiden Hall as the starting linebackers, with Braylon Johnson at the STAR position.
Wake Forest's unofficial starting secondary consists of cornerbacks Deuce Blades II and Ashaad Williams, free safety Rushaun Tongue and strong safety Davaughn Patterson.
Aiden Hall recorded a career-high 73 tackles, eight tackles for loss and three passes defended as a starter in 2025.

coaching_changes.fact: Jake Dickert is in his second season as Wake Forest's head coach after being hired on Dec. 18, 2024.
Rob Ezell is Wake Forest's offensive coordinator, and Dan Enos is co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
Scottie Hazelton is the defensive coordinator, while Freddie Banks is co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach.
Dyrell Roberts joined Wake Forest as wide receivers coach for the 2026 season after coaching East Carolina's receivers from 2023 through 2025.
